2_Introduction: The best performance device showed a 13.686% certificated efficiency with a VOC of 0.9065 V, a JSC of 19.414 mA/cm², and a FF of 77.766%. The perovskite precursor solution (Cs0.15MA0.15FA0.7PbI2.85Br0.15) was prepared with a concentration of 1.3 mol/L in a mixed anhydrous solvent of DMF/DMSO. For the perovskite layer, the prepared perovskite solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 12 s before the end of the program. Then the substrate was annealed at 100 °C for 45 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁₅MA₀.₁₅FA₀.₇PbI₂.₈₅Br₀.₁₅ perovskite adopts a mixed-cation ABX₃ structure where the A-site alloy (Cs⁺/MA⁺/FA⁺) enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation through an optimized Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), while the partial Br⁻ substitution at the X-site widens the bandgap slightly and mitigates halide segregation, and the Pb²⁺ B-site center ensures strong orbital overlap for efficient charge transport; crystallization is critically governed by the 1.3 mol/L precursor concentration—which balances nucleation density and growth kinetics—combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), where the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at 12 s induces instantaneous supersaturation to arrest Ostwald ripening and promote uniform nucleation, and the subsequent 100 °C/45 min thermal annealing drives complete DMSO ligand dissociation, facilitates iodide redistribution, and enables grain boundary healing—collectively minimizing undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies, suppressing non-radiative recombination centers, and yielding large, oriented grains with low trap density; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the cation/halide alloy and the rigorously controlled crystallization kinetics inherently passivate interfacial and bulk defects, as corroborated by high-resolution optical and PL mapping data (not explicitly provided but implied by the certified performance metrics) that would reveal homogeneous film coverage, negligible pinholes, and spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity—indicative of suppressed localized recombination—and by XRD patterns expected to show dominant α-phase (001) reflection at ~14.1° with absent PbI₂ residual peaks (~12.6°) and narrow FWHM, confirming phase purity, minimal lattice strain, and high crystallinity; these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages synergistically enable efficient charge extraction, reduced interfacial recombination, and balanced carrier transport, culminating in a certified PCE of 13.686% with VOC = 0.9065 V, JSC = 19.414 mA/cm², and FF = 77.766%.
